This example follows the card deck from data format → mapping → tiles → color → labels/theme using a simple gene-expression dataset.

## 1. Load packages

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
```

## 2. Start with a dummy wide gene-expression dataset

Each row is a gene, and each sample is stored in its own column.

```r
wide_df <- data.frame(
  gene = c("TP53", "BRCA1", "EGFR", "MYC", "VEGFA"),
  S1 = c(8.2, 4.1, 6.5, 7.8, 3.9),
  S2 = c(7.4, 5.3, 8.1, 6.9, 4.8),
  S3 = c(6.1, 6.8, 7.2, 8.5, 5.6),
  S4 = c(9.0, 5.9, 6.7, 7.1, 6.3),
  S5 = c(8.6, 4.7, 8.4, 7.6, 5.1)
)

wide_df
```

The table looks like this:

| gene | S1 | S2 | S3 | S4 | S5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP53 | 8.2 | 7.4 | 6.1 | 9.0 | 8.6 |
| BRCA1 | 4.1 | 5.3 | 6.8 | 5.9 | 4.7 |
| EGFR | 6.5 | 8.1 | 7.2 | 6.7 | 8.4 |
| MYC | 7.8 | 6.9 | 8.5 | 7.1 | 7.6 |
| VEGFA | 3.9 | 4.8 | 5.6 | 6.3 | 5.1 |

These values are dummy expression measurements for teaching purposes.

## 3. Convert wide data to long data

For `geom_tile()`, it is convenient to have one sample–gene combination per row.

```r
df <- wide_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -gene,
    names_to = "sample",
    values_to = "expression"
  )

df
```

The resulting structure is:

| sample | gene | expression |
|---|---|---:|
| S1 | TP53 | 8.2 |
| S2 | TP53 | 7.4 |
| S3 | TP53 | 6.1 |
| S4 | TP53 | 9.0 |
| S5 | TP53 | 8.6 |
| ... | ... | ... |

## 4. Map the data with `aes()`

A heatmap needs three mappings:

- `x` → sample
- `y` → gene
- `fill` → the numeric value represented by color

```r
ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = sample,
    y = gene,
    fill = expression
  )
)
```

This only sets up the plot. No tiles are drawn yet.

## 5. Draw the heatmap cells with `geom_tile()`

```r
ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = sample,
    y = gene,
    fill = expression
  )
) +
  geom_tile()
```

Each row in the long-format dataset becomes one tile in the heatmap.

## 6. Control the color scale

`fill` maps expression values to color. A continuous gradient is appropriate here because `expression` is numeric.

```r
ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = sample,
    y = gene,
    fill = expression
  )
) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#F8F4E9",
    high = "#B9A5E3"
  )
```

Lower expression values are shown with lighter colors and higher expression values with darker colors.

## 7. Add labels and a theme

```r
ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = sample,
    y = gene,
    fill = expression
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#F8F4E9",
    high = "#B9A5E3"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gene expression heatmap",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Gene",
    fill = "Expression"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Complete script

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

wide_df <- data.frame(
  gene = c("TP53", "BRCA1", "EGFR", "MYC", "VEGFA"),
  S1 = c(8.2, 4.1, 6.5, 7.8, 3.9),
  S2 = c(7.4, 5.3, 8.1, 6.9, 4.8),
  S3 = c(6.1, 6.8, 7.2, 8.5, 5.6),
  S4 = c(9.0, 5.9, 6.7, 7.1, 6.3),
  S5 = c(8.6, 4.7, 8.4, 7.6, 5.1)
)

df <- wide_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -gene,
    names_to = "sample",
    values_to = "expression"
  )

ggplot(
  df,
  aes(
    x = sample,
    y = gene,
    fill = expression
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#F8F4E9",
    high = "#B9A5E3"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gene expression heatmap",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Gene",
    fill = "Expression"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## The basic pattern

```r
ggplot(data, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile()
```

For a typical gene-expression table:

```text
wide table
    ↓
pivot_longer()
    ↓
sample + gene + expression
    ↓
aes(x = sample, y = gene, fill = expression)
    ↓
geom_tile()
    ↓
color scale + labels + theme
```

## Note

This is a plotting example, not a full gene-expression workflow. Real RNA-seq heatmaps are often made from transformed or normalized values rather than raw counts.
